Earthquake · next 30 days

Where a large earthquake is more likely in the next 30 days

Earthquakes cannot be predicted. This forecast gives the chance of at least one magnitude 6+ earthquake in each 2° grid cell of the world over the next 30 days, so you can see where the odds are higher than usual.

About this forecast

A chance is not an alarm: a 20% chance still means that, of five such 30-day periods, four would pass without an M6+ earthquake in that cell. Compare a cell with others.

What the model is
Boosted trees over each cell’s long-term M5+ rate and its aftershock-style clustering after recent earthquakes nearby, combined with GEAR1, a published global model of long-term earthquake rates from crustal strain and past seismicity (Bird et al. 2015)
How it tested, 2023–2025
Across every cell, a cell that went on to have an M6+ earthquake was ranked above one that did not 96.9% (95% interval 96.4%–97.3%) of the time (a second look at those years).
The harder question
Among recently active cells only, where telling cells apart is hardest: 76.9% (95% interval 73.5%–79.9%).
Calibration in the test
It forecast 13% more cells with an M6+ earthquake than there were (ratio 1.13, 95% interval 1.03–1.26).
